Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 14 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Access Equality Index 2026: Goa Tops; AP Ranks Second and Leads Socio-Economic Security In November 2026, the Centre for New Economics Studies (CNES) at O.P. Jindal Global University (Haryana), released the Access Equality Index (AEI) 2026, evaluating access to essential public services across 28 Indian states, with Goa topping the index at 0.68, followed by Andhra Pradesh (AP) at 0.66 and Sikkim at 0.63. • AP ranked first nationally in the socio-economic security pillar with 0.69, followed by Goa with 0.50. AP emerged as the highest-ranked major state in the overall index. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Access Equality Index 2026 released ✓ Released By: CNES, O.P. Jindal Global University, Haryana ✓ Top States: Goa (0.68); AP (0.66); Sikkim (0.63) ✓ Total States Assessed: 28 ✓ Assessment: 5 dimensions, 23 categories and 60 indicators ✓ AP: Ranked first in Socio-Economic Security (0.69). About Access Equality Index (AEI) 2026: Methodology: The index evaluates five foundational pillars using 60 indicators across 23 categories, assigning equal weight to each pillar. Pillars: The five pillars cover Basic Amenities (water, sanitation, housing and energy), Healthcare (medical facilities, maternal care and affordability), Education (infrastructure, enrolment and learning resources), Socio-Economic Security (employment, banking, credit, insurance and pensions) and Legal Services (police, courts, prisons and free legal aid). Framework: The 4As framework covers Availability, Affordability, Approachability and Appropriateness, ensuring balanced assessment across all five pillars. Aspirants: Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh (UP), Madhya Pradesh (MP), Odisha and Assam were identified among the states in the bottom Aspirant tier. AP: Despite ranking 13th nationally in per capita income,AP secured 2nd position in providing equitable access to opportunities and essential services. • The state recorded the highest positive access-score differential of +0.15 (actual score: 0.66; income-predicted score: 0.51), ahead of Kerala (+0.07) and Himachal Pradesh (HP) (+0.06). Top 5 Performing States at AEI 2026: Rank State Score 1 Goa 0.68 2 Andhra Pradesh (AP) 0.66 3 Sikkim 0.63 4 Kerala 0.60 5 Tamil Nadu (TN) 0.57 CCWM1.DCu64_kOjWOTjQKM5L47q9Wr-Ky5gzPSU9iHqzz7XIN6osj790-VEAalLlbcV5v6D6kyHD_0Ii6awI_cXPXMbXBrqVtt_Q

Abdul Nazeer Capital – Amaravati National Park (NP) – Sri Venkateswara NP NITI Aayog Launches Report on “Impact Assessment of PLI Schemes” In November 2026, the National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) released the report titled “Impact Assessment of PLI Schemes”, presenting a sector-wise assessment of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme across all 14 sectors notified by the Government of India (GoI). • The report highlighted that the PLI schemes in 14 sectors had completed 58% of their combined implementation period (as of March 2026), with 42% still remaining. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Release of Report “Impact Assessment of PLI Schemes” ✓ Released by: NITI Aayog ✓ Knowledge Partner: IIM-Ahmedabad (Gujarat) ✓ Key Parameters: Investment, additional production, exports, and employment generation ✓ Total Investment: Rs 2.4 lakh crore (76% of the total target) ✓ Production and Sales: Rs 22.66 lakh crore (64% of the target output) ✓ Employment: 8.49 lakh people (28% of full-tenure target). About the Report: Knowledge Partner: The newly released report was prepared in partnership with the Indian Institute of Management (IIM-Ahmedabad), Gujarat as the knowledge partner. Assessment: The report assesses the impact of the scheme on the key parameters such as: investment, additional production, exports, and employment generation, based on sector-wise collection of firm-level data shared by implementing Ministries, supplemented by industry-level inputs from authenticated sources. Categorization of Outcomes: The report has categorized sectoral outcomes into four main groups: on- track (marked green), partial impact (marked yellow), Insufficient evidence of impact (marked orange), and data unavailable (marked light blue); providing a structured and comparative overview of the scheme’s progress across sectors. Key Findings: Investment: As per the report, Together, PLI Schemes attracted investments of Rs 2.4 lakh crore (achieving 76% of the set investment target), generating production and sales worth Rs 22.66 lakh crore (64% of the target output) across all the 14 sectors. Employment Generation: As of March 2026, these schemes generated employment for 8.49 lakh people, representing 28% of the full-tenure target of 30.18 lakh jobs. On-Track PLI Schemes: The report showed that nearly 70% of the targeted segment i.e. PLI schemes in 4 sectors which includes Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (LSEM); pharmaceutical drugs; telecommunications and networking products, and food products, have been “on-track”.

Key Recommendations: The report emphasized greater attention to sector-specific bottlenecks, workforce skills, innovation and domestic value addition. • It further urged for greater industry participation in setting sector-specific targets, particularly in industry with long gestation periods and uncertain demand. About Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes: Launch: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes were introduced in 2020, initially covering mobile phones, specified electronic components and critical pharmaceutical ingredients. Expansion: Subsequently extended to 14 key sectors, including Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (LSEM), pharmaceuticals, bulk drugs, medical devices, Information Technology (IT) hardware, automobiles, telecom, textiles, food processing, drones, white goods, solar photovoltaic modules, advanced chemistry cell batteries and speciality steel. Disbursement: So far, the GoI has disbursed Rs 35, 354 crore to companies, accounting for 18.51% of the total budget (Rs 1.91 lakh crore) allocated for the scheme. KVS-Samvaad Parent Connect App and Web Portal: • Objective: Strengthens communication between Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) and parents through digital access to attendance, academic progress, results, learning resources and records, online leave applications, and parent-teacher communication, reducing paperwork and school visits. • Services: Enables parents to apply online for Bonafide Certificates and Children Education Allowance (CEA) certificates. KVS Alumni Connect Portal: The platform enables former KV students to reconnect with their schools and batchmates, share experiences, mentor current students, provide career guidance and contribute to institutional development. About Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS): Establishment: Founded in 1963 as “Central Schools”, following the recommendations of the Second Central Pay Commission (1957–59), KVS was formally registered as a society on 15 December 1965 under the Societies Registration Act, 1860. Structure: KVS is an autonomous organisation under the Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), MoE, headquartered in New Delhi, Delhi. RBI’s Directions on Domestic Money Transfer: Legal Basis: The RBI issued the new directions under Section 18 read with Section 10(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007, consolidating its earlier instructions issued in October 2011 and July 2024. Applicable to: The directions apply to all Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs), including Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Urban Co-Operative Banks (UCBs), State Co-operative Banks (StCB) and District Central Co- operative Banks (DCCB) as well as authorised payment system operators. Cash Pay-Out service: Banks are permitted to facilitate the transfer of money from a customer’s bank account to beneficiaries who do not have bank accounts through ATMs (Automated Teller Machine), Business Correspondents (BCs) or other authorised payment channels. • The maximum transfer limit is Rs 10,000 per transaction, subject to an overall monthly ceiling of Rs 25,000 per beneficiary.
